missing_units.surface: Human lifecycle routes (POST /sandboxes/{sid}/pause|resume|snapshot|restore, DELETE /sandboxes/{sid}, and the /ui equivalents) racing the agent and human paths that do NOT take AgentBox._lifecycle: call_tool/_call_tool/_run_tool exec and file tools, _snapshot (auto snapshot before destructive actions), decide (approved run), import_file/export_file/upload, takeover/handback, GUI bursts open/close, expire_stale and extract/capture paths
missing_units.boundary: Agent and human actions versus sandbox lifecycle state (F6 fix, PR #18). _lifecycle (service.py:500-505) is a per-sandbox mutex taken only by pause/resume/snapshot/restore/delete (service.py:507-540); call_tool, decide, import_file, takeover and the burst code never take it, so a tool exec, an approval decide or a pre-destructive snapshot can still run against a container that restore is replacing or delete is removing. Also: restore/snapshot hold the lock across a multi-second docker commit while log_human and end_desktop run inside it (human request threads and the Starlette threadpool can pile up behind one sandbox), self._life_locks (service.py:90) is a dict that grows per sandbox id and is never pruned, and SandboxManager.restore now refuses status 'deleted' (check that every other manager method that takes a snapshot, resume or exec has the same state guard). Invariant: after restore or delete returns, no agent or approved action writes to, snapshots, or records results for the old container or a deleted sandbox, no snapshot row or image is orphaned or attributed to the wrong container_id, and a lifecycle call cannot be starved or deadlocked by a tool call, takeover or burst close that holds _snap_locks, gui_lock or the per-sandbox concurrency slots.

missing_units.reason: PR #18 (F6) changed the lifecycle serialisation and restore-of-deleted handling but no run-5 ledger unit owns it. The seven units cover the body cap, disk guard, GUI lease, XRes, desktop WS, prune and approval-row compaction. The only mutual exclusion added is a lock that the agent-facing and decide paths never acquire (grep shows _lifecycle used only at service.py:507-539), so the fix's actual coverage against concurrent call_tool, decide, import_file and auto-snapshots, and the lock's own availability and leak properties, have not been reviewed in the current tree.

missing_units.surface: POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/exec (and any tool whose argument text reaches Policy.decide and preview_command) with a long or adversarially shaped command, run on the tool_pool thread before any approval exists, plus the approval-card render of the same text
missing_units.boundary: Agent to control-plane availability: pure-Python, CPU-bound policy and preview parsing of an attacker-sized command (up to the 8 MiB AGENTBOX_MAX_BODY; no per-command or per-argument length cap exists, grep finds only max_body_bytes) holds the GIL shared with the event loop and every human request thread. The h-approvals hunter measured Policy.decide at 4.96 s for a 128 KiB 'x;' command, growing at least linearly, and up to 4 such calls run concurrently per sandbox on the 32-thread tool_pool, across sandboxes. Invariant: no agent-supplied command or argument can make policy evaluation, _split_segments, simple_programs/shlex passes, _raw_hits or the preview glob/walk expansion cost more than a small bounded amount of CPU, memory or container-side exec time before the call is rejected or queued, and the human API stays responsive while it runs.
missing_units.subsystem: agentbox/policy.py#decide/_words/command_names/_raw_hits/simple_programs/has_bash_comment + agentbox/preview.py#preview_command/_split_segments + agentbox/sandbox.py#_expand/_walk (container-side glob and find, no timeout) + agentbox/service.py#call_tool/_call_tool/_logged_args + agentbox/api.py#tool route
missing_units.attack_class: Resource exhaustion: algorithmic complexity and worker starvation

excluded_blocks.reason: Container-output reader caps are run-4 N3 (needs_validation, not re-hunted); this unit is about CPU spent on agent-supplied input, not container output.

missing_units.reason: Reported uncovered by the h-approvals hunter with a local measurement and owned by no unit: the pre-auth body-cap unit stops at transport size, the approval-row unit covers storage compaction after the call, and the disk-guard unit covers disk. None of them evaluates whether an 8 MiB command body is a CPU/GIL starvation vector for human threads, or whether a length cap belongs before policy.decide. The measured 128 KiB cost makes it a concrete, bounded-effort hunt with a clear invariant.

missing_units.surface: AuditLog._lock as a global contention point reachable by agent-grown table size and by unauthenticated traffic: GET /ui/audit (polled every 3 s by templates/sandbox.html), GET /ui/verify, GET /audit/verify, AuditLog.recent (unindexed COUNT(*) WHERE sandbox_id), AuditLog.verify (fetchall of the whole table, audit.py:336-350), AuditLog.list, versus every AuditLog.append/insert_record from agent tool calls and every fail-closed log_human; plus the unauthenticated POST /login failure throttle (web.py:93-114) and extract_novnc single-flight (sandbox_desktop.py:174)
missing_units.boundary: Agent and unauthenticated clients to human availability and audit evidence. The audit table grows with agent tool calls (until disk_low), and recent() and verify() scan it while holding the same lock append needs; human state-changing routes use log_human, which fails closed with 503, so a long hold turns into refused human actions, and verify loads the whole table into memory. Hunter measurement: 0.034 s (recent) and 0.84 s (verify) per 100k rows. The F8 login throttle uses one global 60 s window with 5 logged failures (an unauthenticated client can use up the budget so later real failures are only counted), and F5 extract_novnc holds a global lock across docker create and tar extraction for every unauthenticated /static/novnc request while the negative cache is cold. Invariant: no sequence of agent calls or unauthenticated requests can hold AuditLog._lock or a shared lock long enough to make log_human fail closed for the human, make verify exhaust memory, or suppress the audit evidence of a credential-guessing attempt beyond the documented suppressed_before count.
missing_units.subsystem: agentbox/audit.py#recent/verify/list/append/insert_record/_lock + agentbox/web.py#note_login_failure/audit and verify routes + agentbox/api.py#/audit/verify + agentbox/sandbox_desktop.py#extract_novnc/_NOVNC_LOCK + agentbox/templates/sandbox.html (3 s poll)

missing_units.reason: Reported uncovered by the h-ws hunter with measurements. The prune/retention unit checks tamper evidence, not read-side lock holds, and the disk-guard unit bounds growth rather than the cost of scanning what is allowed to accumulate (every pruning is manual, host CLI only). PR #18's F5 (extract_novnc) and F8 (login throttle) changes also have no unit: the pre-auth unit covers body framing only, and the WS unit stops at accept().
